q: Pico Turquino, Cuba's highest mountain, is in which mountain range?
explain: Pico Turquino (about 1,970 m) rises in the Sierra Maestra in south-eastern Cuba.

q: Which stretch of water, only about 150 km wide at its narrowest, separates Cuba from the Florida Keys?
explain: The Straits of Florida link the Gulf of Mexico to the Atlantic, between Cuba and the Florida Keys.

q: What is the largest lake in El Salvador, which fills the crater of an ancient volcano?
explain: Lake Ilopango lies just east of San Salvador. Lake Atitlán is in Guatemala, Lake Yojoa in Honduras.

q: The Gulf of Fonseca, an inlet of the Pacific Ocean, is shared by El Salvador, Nicaragua and which other country?
explain: Honduras sits between El Salvador and Nicaragua on the Gulf of Fonseca, so all three share its shores.

q: Which famous scientist studied the animals of Ecuador's Galápagos Islands, which helped him form his ideas about evolution?
explain: Charles Darwin visited the Galápagos in 1835 on the ship HMS Beagle.

q: Which great mountain range runs through the middle of Ecuador?
explain: The Andes run down the whole west side of South America, right through Ecuador. Its capital, Quito, sits high in the Andes.
Senegal is on the far west of Africa, on the Atlantic coast.

q: Which huge desert lies to the north of Senegal?
explain: The Sahara covers much of North Africa, including most of Senegal's northern neighbour, Mauritania.
